analysis:
The PR changes only docs/provider/two-mac-cluster.md. The patch (head lines 49-73) adds a 'cluster waitlist' section describing `darkbloom waitlist cluster` and a pre-pairing waitlist check in `darkbloom cluster`. The supplied base units (lines 449-1312) are unchanged text in a later part of the file and contain no edits. No code, configuration or control changes are in the supplied evidence, so I found no regression in A-001, A-008, A-015, A-016, TB-002, TB-011 or T-041.

The documentation makes these claims:
- The waitlist is account-level and sends nothing about the Macs.
- It requires `darkbloom login`.
- Already-paired Macs are never asked, so existing pairs keep working through updates and restarts.

The following are not verified and are not demonstrated by this PR:
- The enforcement code, its auth, and the backend/coordinator waitlist endpoints are not in the supplied evidence and appear to be platform-owned.
- Whether the 'already paired' exemption is enforced client-side only is unknown. If it is, it is a business gating control and not a security boundary, and nothing here treats it as one.
- The waitlist command's use of A-008 provider tokens and its data minimisation ('sending nothing about your Macs') should be checked against the implementation (CLI source and cli-reference.md) in a code-level review.

The unchanged base text covers cluster approvals, cable-only local serving, the encrypted SSD prefix cache (T-041) and update flows. None of it is altered by this PR. The threat model may need a note if waitlist gating is added as a trust control, but nothing in this diff requires one.
